paper.title: Hierarchy-boosted funnel learning for identifying semiconductors with ultralow lattice thermal conductivity
paper.research_summary: The paper proposes a hierarchy-boosted funnel learning (HiBoFL) framework that integrates unsupervised and supervised learning to efficiently identify semiconductors with ultralow lattice thermal conductivity (κL), circumventing large-scale brute-force ab initio calculations. It uses unsupervised clustering on a high-throughput dataset to narrow the search space, performs low-cost phonon-elasticity-thermal (PET) model-based high-throughput calculations on selected clusters to build a labeled local database, trains a CatBoost classifier to predict ultralow κL, and conducts interpretable SHAP analysis to uncover structural descriptors governing κL—especially discovering Lmin as a new factor influencing structural anharmonicity and phonon lifetime.

task.task_name_raw: identifying semiconductors with ultralow lattice thermal conductivity
task.objective: Identify semiconductors with ultralow lattice thermal conductivity (κL) for potential thermoelectric applications
output_goal: list of candidate semiconductors with ultralow κL
discovery of new factor (Lmin) governing structural anharmonicity

evidence.text: Here, we propose a novel hierarchy-boosted funnel learning (HiBoFL) framework, which is successfully applied to identify semiconductors with ultralow lattice thermal conductivity (κL).
We then apply this HiBoFL framework to efﬁciently identify semiconductors with ultralow κL as shown in Fig. 1b.

As a compelling demonstration, this framework has been successfully applied to identify semiconductors with ultralow κL, which circumvents large-scale brute-force ab initio calculations without clear objectives.

stages.stage_name_raw: obtaining material dataset from Materials Project database
stages.stage_goal: Acquire initial theoretical dataset of semiconductors for screening

evidence.text: Initially, we start by acquiring all the materials from the MP database based on its API, resulting in a total of 1,54,718 entries saved in a JSON ﬁle as the Python dictionary object.

stages.stage_goal: Narrow down the material pool using thermodynamic, electronic, and computational constraints

evidence.text: Ultimately, through excluding the materials containing hydrogen, lanthanides, and actinides, and conducting structural analysis, we further obtain 2675 three-dimensional (3D) crystal structures without calculation errors. These materials constitute the first-level dataset for our in-depth investigations.

stages.stage_name_raw: unsupervised learning for clustering materials with similar κL
stages.stage_goal: Identify problem-specific clusters likely to contain materials with ultralow κL
stage_output: two problem-specific clusters (C1 and C2) containing 704 materials

evidence.text: Since the materials with a high likelihood of possessing relatively low κL tend to group into the two clusters of C1 and C2, the exploration scope for ﬁnding materials with low κL is reduced from 2675 materials to 704 materials, narrowing by approximately three-quarters. As a result, these two problem-speciﬁc clusters (C1 and C2) further constitute our second-level dataset.

stages.stage_name_raw: high-throughput calculation (HTC) of κPET on problem-specific clusters
stages.stage_goal: Assign property labels (κPET values) to materials in C1 and C2 using low-cost PET model
stage_output: 661 labeled materials with κPET values at 300 K stored in local MongoDB database

evidence.text: Given the success of unsupervised learning in signiﬁcantly reducing the broad material search space, it has become feasible to further extend the second-level dataset into a labeled repository of thermal conductivity through HTC at affordable computational costs. Based on the PET empirical equation within the high-throughput framework, we derive the κPET values at 300 K ignoring the anisotropy for materials in the second-level dataset...

The basic information and corresponding κPET values of the resulting 661 materials are then stored in a local database using MongoDB64, serving as a valuable repository to retrieve data and prioritize detailed theoretical and experimental investigations.

stages.stage_name_raw: training CatBoost classifier on labeled local database
stages.stage_goal: Train supervised classification model to predict ultralow κL (κPET ≤ 2 W/mK)

evidence.text: After labeling the materials in the second-level dataset based on our HTC framework to obtain the local database, we develop interpretable supervised classiﬁcation models to predict ultralow κL for efﬁciently by-passing the complex ab initio calculations, which can further reﬁne the coarse result of unsupervised learning and provide greater robustness.

To avoid the curse of dimensionality, we perform feature selection using the model-based wrapper method and Pearson correlation method... As a result, the performances of the optimal CatBoost classiﬁcation model are characterized by the ROC curve and the confusion matrix (Fig. 6b), showing its great ability in classifying semiconductors with ultralow κL due to the high ROC AUC (0.94), accuracy (0.90), precision (0.89), recall (0.90) and F1-score (0.89).

stage_output: ROC AUC = 0.94, accuracy = 0.90, precision = 0.89, recall = 0.90, F1-score = 0.89

stages.stage_name_raw: screening candidates Cs2SnSe3 and Cs2GeSe3 for in-depth mechanism analysis
stages.stage_goal: Select top candidates from low-κPET list for first-principles validation and mechanistic study

evidence.text: To further validate the results and conduct in-depth analysis of the phonon thermal transport mechanisms, we calculate more precise κL values according to ﬁrst-principles derived force constants and Boltzmann transport theory for the unreported materials Cs2SnSe3 and Cs2GeSe3, which are screened out based on the formula type ranking among the materials with the lowest κPET values.

stages.stage_name_raw: first-principles calculation of κL for Cs2SnSe3 and Cs2GeSe3
stages.stage_goal: Computationally validate ultralow κL and reveal phonon transport mechanisms
stage_output: precise κL values (< 0.25 W/mK at 300 K)
phonon dispersion, PDOS, spectral κL(ω), group velocity, phonon lifetime, COHP analysis

evidence.text: To further validate κPET from the PET empirical equation and investigate the phonon thermal transport mechanisms, we calculated more accurate κL values for Cs2SnSe3 and Cs2SnSe3 by iteratively solving the phonon BTE94,97...

Moreover, these materials all exhibit intrinsically ultralow κL, with values all below 0.25 W/mK in any direction at 300 K, signiﬁcantly lower than the κL (~2.3 W/mK) of the traditional TE material PbTe71.

stages.stage_name_raw: assigning binary labels (ultralow/non-ultralow κL) based on κPET threshold
stages.stage_goal: Generate training labels for supervised classification
stage_output: binary labels: 1 if κPET ≤ 2 W/mK, else 0

evidence.text: Here, materials with κPET not exceeding 2 W/mK are labeled as 1, which are considered to possess ultralow κL; otherwise, they are labeled as 0, signifying non-ultralow κL.

stages.stage_name_raw: interpretable analysis using SHAP to discover Lmin as new factor governing structural anharmonicity
stages.stage_goal: Uncover physical descriptors and mechanisms underlying ultralow κL prediction
stage_output: discovery of Lmin as special descriptor influencing phonon lifetime and structural anharmonicity

evidence.text: A new factor capable of signiﬁcantly reducing κL via enhancing structural anharmonicity is discovered, eventually building a bridge between the ML model interpretability and ﬁrst-principles analysis.

The special factor Lmin is discovered to show a unique inﬂuence on structural anharmonicity, leading to the difference of phonon lifetime in Cs2GeSe3 and Cs2SnSe3, in agreement with the ﬁrst-principles analysis.
